subject: Agriculture
title: Dam Removal Movement
description: Learn Dam Removal Movement in one minute.

hook.text: After a century of dam building, some countries are now tearing dams down. The benefits surprised everyone.

buildup.text: Old dams lose storage to sediment buildup, require expensive repairs, and block fish migration.

discovery.text: Removing two dams on the Elwha River in Washington restored salmon runs within five years.

twist.text: Over 1,700 dams have been removed in the US since 1912. Most were small and obsolete.

climax.text: Free-flowing rivers carry sediment to coastlines and floodplains, rebuilding landscapes that dams had starved.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best infrastructure decision is subtraction.

quiz.question: What benefit did removing dams on the Elwha River produce?
options: Salmon runs were restored within five years

details.summary: The dam removal movement advocates tearing down obsolete, dangerous, or ecologically harmful dams to restore river ecosystems. This topic covers why dams are being removed, the environmental benefits observed, and how the movement challenges traditional water infrastructure thinking.
details.whyItMatters: While dams provide irrigation and hydropower, aging dams increasingly fail to deliver benefits while blocking fish migration, trapping sediment, and degrading downstream ecosystems critical for agriculture and biodiversity.
takeaways: Over 1,900 dams have been removed in the US since 1912, with the pace accelerating
The Elwha River in Washington saw salmon return within months of dam removal
Removing obsolete dams can restore floodplain fertility and sediment delivery to farms

faq.question: Why are dams being removed?
faq.answer: Many dams are old, structurally unsafe, and no longer economically productive. They block fish migration, trap sediment that starves downstream deltas, alter water temperatures, and degrade river ecosystems while providing diminishing irrigation or power benefits.

faq.question: What happens to ecosystems after a dam is removed?
faq.answer: Rivers often recover remarkably quickly. Fish populations return, sediment flows restore downstream habitats, water temperatures normalize, and riparian vegetation regrows. The Elwha River in Washington state is a celebrated success story of rapid ecological recovery.
